finding.title: Split 4 oversized hand-written test files in features/profiles/presentation (805-1079 lines) — over the AG-3 400-line cap
finding.why: parent_pin_keypad_dialog_test.dart (1079 lines), parent_settings_screen_l1_test.dart (999), parent_track_management_screen_l1_test.dart (902), and profile_picker_screen_l1_test.dart (805) each run 2-2.7x over the 400-line AG-3 cap, each covering many unrelated scenario groups (e.g. parent_settings mixes the tutor-permission-tile matrix, the Adjust-Points dialog, and the Pending-Prizes subtitle in one file/one main()), which is harder to navigate and increases merge-conflict surface on churned files.
finding.recommendation: Split each by scenario group, mirroring the ppNN/tsN per-scenario file convention already used elsewhere in this same directory (e.g. peel Adjust-Points-dialog and Pending-Prizes tests out of parent_settings_screen_l1_test.dart into their own files).
acceptance_criteria: `find learning_tracker/test -name '*.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'` reports zero files under test/features/profiles/presentation/.

finding.title: Catch and log exceptions around TutorPinService calls in the PIN entry/setup async handlers
finding.why: _onPinComplete (gate) and _onConfirmPinEntered (setup) wrap their await in try/finally with no catch clause. TutorPinService.verifyTutorPin/setTutorPin only converts PinLockoutException — an underlying secure-storage failure (a real class of Android keystore/PlatformException issue this environment has hit before per the App Check debug-token flakiness on wipes) propagates as a raw, uncaught exception. Because _onPinComplete is invoked fire-and-forget (not awaited) from _appendDigit, the failure is swallowed by whatever global handler exists, with zero AppLogger call from this site and zero user feedback: _isVerifying resets to false in the finally block but _errorMessage stays null and _digits stays at 4 filled dots, leaving the user staring at a stalled numpad with no explanation and no way to retype until they notice backspace still works.
finding.recommendation: Add a typed catch around the await that logs via AppLogger and sets a generic, localized _errorMessage (consistent with EH-2's 'no raw exception reaches presentation').
acceptance_criteria: _onPinComplete and _onConfirmPinEntered both have a catch block that calls AppLogger.instance.error and sets a localized _errorMessage
a test that makes the stubbed TutorPinService throw confirms the screen shows an error state instead of a silent stall

finding.title: Override the injectable LocalDayClock in backup_sync_section_l1_test.dart's relative-time assertions

evidence.quote: final now = DateTime.now(); / final lastSynced = now.subtract(const Duration(seconds: 30));

finding.why: _formatTimeAgo reads DateTimeFactory.nowLocal(), which resolves through the overridable localDayClockProvider — a FakeLocalDayClock already exists in lib/core/time/local_day_clock.dart for exactly this purpose. This file never overrides it: it seeds 'just now'/'Xm ago' assertions from real DateTime.now() at 5 call sites (lines 155, 179, 201, 227, 657), then the widget independently re-reads the clock a pump later. Today's margins (e.g. a 30s buffer under the 60s 'just now' cliff) make an actual flake unlikely, but the suite is non-deterministic by construction and the gap between test-now and widget-build-now is unbounded on a loaded/slow CI runner.
finding.recommendation: In _buildHarness, call useLocalDayClock(FakeLocalDayClock(fixedInstant)) (or override localDayClockProvider) and derive lastSynced from that same fixed instant, removing the wall-clock dependency entirely.
acceptance_criteria: backup_sync_section_l1_test.dart's relative-time tests construct lastSyncedAt from a fixed instant and override localDayClockProvider/useLocalDayClock to that same instant.
The suite still passes with no bare DateTime.now() feeding a time-relative text assertion.

finding.title: Stop testing RewardSaveNoTrack/RewardSaveDuplicateThreshold — both sealed variants are unreachable post-DEC-32/GA-3
finding.rule: TQ-8 (tests must exercise the branch they claim) / Fowler speculative generality

evidence.quote:
// Manually inject a track into the state so setGlobalReward respects
      // the parameter. We can do this by mutating state via the notifier's
test('returns empty list when per-track mode but no track selected', () async {

finding.why: reward_config_controller.dart's bootstrap() hardcodes `tracks: const []` (comment: 'the form is always global and no track list is loaded'), so RewardForm.usesGlobalLadder is always true and the per-track/no-track-selected code in saveReward() is unreachable; separately, GA-3 removed the duplicate-threshold rejection entirely ('the old RewardSaveDuplicateThreshold result is no longer returned'). Despite that, 3 tests in reward_config_controller_test.dart claim to cover 'allows non-global when tracks is non-empty', 'per-track mode but no track selected', and 'RewardSaveNoTrack' but either exercise the identical tracks-empty branch under a different name or never call saveReward() at all (they assert on a hand-built RewardForm instead); a 4th test in reward_configuration_screen_l1_test.dart renders UI for a RewardSaveDuplicateThreshold result the real controller can never produce. A future revert or refactor that mangles these dead branches would ship with zero real regression coverage despite the suite appearing to test exactly that.
finding.recommendation: Remove the dead tracks/selectedTrackId/RewardSaveNoTrack/RewardSaveDuplicateThreshold machinery (and the screen's switch arm for it) now that DEC-32/GA-3 are final, deleting these 4 tests with it; or if per-track rewards are coming back, rewrite the tests to actually seed RewardForm.tracks through a real bootstrap path.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn "RewardSaveNoTrack\|RewardSaveDuplicateThreshold" lib/` returns no hits after cleanup, or a new test drives RewardForm.tracks non-empty via the real controller and asserts the branch.
No test in reward_config_controller_test.dart asserts on a hand-constructed RewardForm as a substitute for calling the notifier method the test's group() claims to cover.

finding.title: Tighten the granularity and pace-floor assertions in step_chazara_goal_l1_test.dart and edit_track_and_detail_l1_test.dart to match what their own titles/comments claim

evidence.quote:
// Just verifying the value "1" is visible (loading completed).
        expect(find.text('1'), findsWidgets);

finding.why: The chazara-goal test titled 'selecting coarse (perek) emits paceGranularity=perek' taps the 'Perakim' segment then only asserts goal.rawLearningUnit isNotNull — but _paceGranularity is set to a non-null default in initState() before any tap, so the assertion passes identically whether or not the tap actually changed anything. The edit-track test titled 'pace increment button is disabled when paceValue is 1 (minimum)' never inspects the stepper button's onPressed at all (its own comment admits 'Just verifying the value "1" is visible') — floor enforcement for EditTrackScreen's pace stepper is untested anywhere in the tree (grepped for 'remove_rounded'/'onPressed.*isNull' in the sibling edit_track_screen_l1_test.dart: no match).
finding.recommendation: Assert goal.rawLearningUnit equals the coarse key's storage value ('perek') rather than isNotNull. In the edit-track test, find the decrement IconButton (ancestor of Icons.remove_rounded) and assert its onPressed is null at paceValue==1, then non-null after an increment.
acceptance_criteria: Granularity test asserts goal.rawLearningUnit == the expected coarse key, not just non-null
Pace-floor test asserts tester.widget<IconButton>(...).onPressed is null at value 1 and non-null after incrementing
